subject: ICT
title: How Many are Left?
subtitle: Taking away with the magician's hat
hero_picture: Two blue mother birds looking sadly into a nest with only 2 eggs while a cat sits nearby, other birds flying above.

sections.heading: The bird's nest
text: 'Oh! There were 4 eggs!' cries the mother bird.
Now there are only 2 eggs in the nest.
sections.caption: The mother bird's nest
sections.picture: Two worried blue birds looking into a nest that has only 2 small eggs.

sections.heading: Take away
text: Taking away makes the number smaller.
sections.caption: Before and after
sections.picture: A nest with 4 eggs on one side and the same nest with 2 eggs on the other side, an arrow between them (no text).

sections.heading: Fruits on a plate
text: There are 6 oranges on a plate.
sections.caption: Taking oranges away
sections.picture: Six oranges on a plate and a child's hand taking 2 away, 4 left on the plate.

sections.heading: The magician's hat −
text: Click the hat: some stars go in and out.
Count the stars left under the hat and answer.
sections.caption: Magic hat takes stars
sections.picture: A green chalkboard with gold stars, a purple magician's hat taking some stars away (no numbers).

sections.heading: Share and count
sections.caption: Sharing biscuits
sections.picture: Children sharing biscuits: a boy gives 3 of his 5 biscuits to his friends and has 2 left.

rhyme: Four little eggs in a cosy nest,
Two rolled away, where's the rest?
Four take two, how many stay?
activity: Put 7 spoons on the table. Take away 3. Count how many are left and write 7 − 3 = 4.
talk: How many eggs were there at first?
How many biscuits did Hari keep?
summary: To find how many are left, we take away and count what remains.

questions.prompt: 4 eggs; 2 are lost. How many are left?
6 oranges; 2 are taken. How many are left?
5 biscuits; 3 are given. How many are left?
When we take away, the number becomes...
In the game we count the stars...
questions.explanation: Count the stars left under the hat.
